> **Narrowed 2026-10-14 (Sue).** An open issue describes exactly the remaining work (backlog-workflow rule).
>
> **Resolved so far:** Phase I landed: 634db2697 (lsms_library/recall.py, RecallRecord, ll.recall(), 20 countries/*/_/recall.yml, attach in _finalize_result), 48c97caaf (dict-subclass), 3989a7281 (#873: attrs['recall'] survives Feature()), 1446e4c1b (Burkina 2014 passages).
>
> **Remaining (this issue):** Phase II per .coder/charter-recall-windows.md:146,203-215: a RecallHeterogeneityWarning in feature._attach_carried_attrs modelled on PopulationHeterogeneityWarning; period= using RecallRecord.total_exposure_days with Contract B; an explicit refusal on food_prices.
>
> **Decision for @ligon:** Ship period= with coverage at 28 of 67 cells under Contract B (typed raise from Country(), degrade+warn from Feature()): yes/no?

---
*Original text, kept for the evidence:*

Nothing records a table's recall window, so summed expenditures mix reference periods across waves, countries and food/non-food (GhanaLSS food is 6 x 5 days; `RecallWindow` is per-row and Togo-only)

`food_expenditures` returns a number whose reference period is nowhere recorded. For GhanaLSS 2016-17 it is **30 days** -- six five-day recalls collected at the 2nd..7th of seven visits, tiling days 1-30 of a 35-day cycle (GLSS7 Main Report, "Interviewer Workload"; now documented in `GhanaLSS/_/CONTENTS.org`, "The repeated-visit design, wave by wave"). For a 7-day-recall country it is 7 days. Nothing in the API, the schema, or `df.attrs` says which, so summing or pooling across waves or countries silently mixes reference windows, and the user has no way to find out short of reading a questionnaire.

The window moves **within** GhanaLSS too, which is what makes this more than a cross-country footnote. Per wave: GLSS4/6/7 field seven visits with the food modules at visits 2..7 (six recalls); GLSS5 fields eleven with purchases at visits 2..11 (ten recalls) and own production at visits 3..11 (**nine**). So in GLSS5 the `s='purchased'` and `s='produced'` totals for the same household cover a different number of intervals -- a within-wave, within-table comparability defect that was invisible until the `visit` level was corrected (#TBD / commit `e55299142`). The 1980s waves are a single "since my last visit" ask, and 1991-92's offsets are still unverified.

The existing mechanism does not cover this. `RecallWindow` (GH #817, `data_info.yml` under `nonfood_expenditures`) is a **per-row column**, populated only by Togo's `nonfood_expenditures`, where EHCVM splits section 9 into five sub-modules with disjoint item-code blocks so `j` determines the window. Three gaps: (a) it is a column, so a **wave-constant** window like GhanaLSS's has no home but a constant column; (b) its value is the instrument's verbatim string and the string -> days conversion lives in a **comment** (`Togo/_/data_scheme.yml`, "annual = Expenditure * 365.25 / days, days = {'7 days': 7, ...}"), so nothing machine-readable can convert or compare it; (c) it has no way to express GhanaLSS's two-level structure, where the *per-observation* window (5 days, at the `visit` grain) and the *summed* window (30 days, and 45 vs 50 in GLSS5) are different numbers.

A recall specification is really three things, and only the first is captured today: the **length** (7 days, 30 days -- what you need to annualise); the **position** of the reference period (the days before the interview, the last completed season, a calendar year -- what you need to align with prices and seasonality); and the **elicitation mode** (single recall, repeated visits, diary). The third is not decoration: GLSS7's frequently-purchased module is diary-assisted -- a literate household member was trained at the first visit to record expenditures, with daily enumerator visits where there was none -- so its measurement error is not comparable with a 30-day unaided recall even at identical length.

**Design is open** and worth settling before anything is built; a sketch of the space, not a proposal:

1. *Extend `RecallWindow` as a column to every expenditure-like table.* One mechanism, travels with the data through concat and `Feature()`, survives caching. But a constant column over 5.3M GhanaLSS rows to carry one fact, no place to record a window for a wave nobody has wired, and no way to say "not stated".
2. *A `recall.yml` sibling of `population.yml`*, per wave x table, surfaced on `df.attrs`. This is the repo's established shape for a documented fact about a wave that is not a data column, and the precedent is exact: `population.yml` solved a structurally identical problem ("two samples that look poolable represent different things") with a per-wave YAML + `source_type` / `confidence` / `source_file` / `locator`, `df.attrs`, and a warning that names the classes and **never drops data** (`PopulationHeterogeneityWarning`, GH #603 -- @ligon declined the fencing variant). It can record absence explicitly, distinguishing "looked, not stated" from "nobody has looked". It moves no cache hash (`.yml` is outside `_BUILD_INPUT_SUFFIXES`; measured for `population.yml`). It cannot express Togo's row-varying case.
3. *Both, with a rule*: config where the window is constant for a (wave, table); the column where it varies within one. Needs a single canonical vocabulary shared by both, or it drifts into two sources of truth.

Whatever the carrier, the **length should be machine-readable**, and the repo already has the pattern: raw instrument string -> canonical label -> numeric factor is exactly how `u` works (`unit_labels.org` -> Preferred Label -> kg factor). Recall windows want the same treatment rather than a dict in a comment.

Two traps for whoever implements it. `_SCHEME_NON_COLUMN_KEYS` (`country.py`) is `{index, materialize, backend, aggregation}`, so a bare `recall:` key added to a `data_scheme.yml` table entry is read as a **required column** and fails the build -- that frozenset must be edited, or the fact must live elsewhere. And a per-row column added to a table changes its cache hash, corpus-wide, where a new `.yml` sibling does not.

Not in scope: annualising anything. The rule this repo already applies -- reported values only, the analyst scales -- should hold; the point is to make the scaling *possible* and the mixing *visible*, not to do it silently.

comments.body:
GLSS3 (GhanaLSS 1991-92) turns out to be the case that decides the shape, and it breaks both candidate designs in the issue body. Established from `1991-92/Documentation/pdf/G3Intman.pdf` §1.9 and corroborated by the survey's own recorded visit dates in `S0B.DTA`:

> "There will be 8 interviewer visits at 2-day intervals to each rural household and 11 interviewer visits at 3-day intervals to each urban household in a cycle."

So the recall window varies **within one wave, by the household's stratum**: urban 10 asks x 3 days = **30 days**, rural 7 asks x 2 days = **14 days**. The visit dates confirm it exactly — urban 11 dates, median gap 3.0 days at every step, 30-day span; rural 8 dates, gap 2.0, 14-day span, visits 9-11 empty.

That is a third pattern, and neither option covers it. Togo's column works because `j` determines the window (disjoint item-code blocks per sub-module); here `j` determines nothing — the **household** does, via a stratum that is not a column of the food module at all. A wave-level `recall.yml` cannot express it either, because there is no single window for the wave.

Worse, it is invisible in the data's shape: there is **one questionnaire**, not two. `G3QPartB.pdf` is a single 9B form with eleven date boxes printed `1st … 11th` and ten question columns, used for both strata; the rural enumerator simply leaves q8-q10 blank. Two forms would have been two file layouts and someone would have noticed. A rural household's blank q8-q10 is indistinguishable from an urban household that was not home unless you have read the fieldwork protocol. The consequence is live: summing `visit` away returns a 30-day figure for an urban household and a 14-day one for a rural household, so an unadjusted urban/rural comparison is off by ~2.14x. GSS itself rescaled by stratum — median published `POV_GH.expfoodc` / raw 9B sum is 11.4 urban against 21.7 rural, versus design factors 365/30 = 12.2 and 365/14 = 26.1.

**Design consequence, following @ligon's rule for this table** — *preserve all detail in `food_acquired`; aggregate, at least by default, in the derived tables*, which is exactly what `visit` already does (kept in the index per D1; summed away by `food_expenditures` / `food_quantities` / `food_prices`, and summed rather than `first()`-ed by `Feature()` via `_ADDITIVE_MEASURE_COLUMNS`):

1. **The window belongs on `food_acquired`, per row.** Togo's *column* mechanism generalises after all — it just is not keyed by `j` in general. GLSS3 keys it by the household. So `RecallWindow` (or a numeric sibling) extends to `food_acquired`, and the wave script stamps it.
2. **The derived tables keep aggregating by default, but must not lose the window silently.** Pooling rows with different windows is the same disease as pooling different populations, and #603 already settled the policy: warn, name the classes, never drop data. `PopulationHeterogeneityWarning` is the model.
3. **"At least by default" wants an opt-out**, and the existing kwarg idiom is the natural home: `food_expenditures(period='day'|'annual')` alongside `units=`, `labels=`, `basis=`, `currency=`. That is what makes the machine-readable length worth storing — without a consumer, the config is documentation, which is how `RecallWindow`'s conversion dict ended up unusable in a comment.
4. **The `recall.yml` sibling still earns a place, for a different job than proposed above**: not to carry the value, but to declare that a wave *has* a window and where it was read from, with `source_type` / `confidence` in the `population.yml` style. Otherwise a table with no `RecallWindow` column is indistinguishable from one nobody has looked at — and GLSS3 is the proof that "nobody has looked" is the common case, since this sat undetected through every prior pass over the wave.

One implementation note for whoever takes it: stamping GLSS3's window needs the household's stratum, which is not in `S9B.DTA`. Reading the cover page directly in the wave script is the sanctioned route for exactly this (CLAUDE.md, "If a wave-level script genuinely needs region for data processing"). Do **not** try to infer the window by counting visits present per household — that conflates the protocol with non-response, which is the very ambiguity the single shared form creates.

Related: the visit-level mapping across all five multi-visit GhanaLSS waves has been corrected (question numbers were being written into `visit`), and `1991-92` also turned out to be dropping `s9bq1` — 16.22% of the wave's recorded food purchase expenditure. Commits `e55299142` and `87c1c252d`; the per-wave design is now in `GhanaLSS/_/CONTENTS.org`, "The repeated-visit design, wave by wave".

**Ruling (@ligon, 2026-10-18)**, from the framework-backlog decision sheet: Yes. Ship `period=` on `food_expenditures`/`food_quantities` under Contract B (a typed raise from `Country()`; degrade plus warning from `Feature()`), and refuse `period=` on `food_prices`. The GLSS3 per-row (stratum-varying) window is out of Phase II scope; file it as its own issue.

Scheduled for the overnight 2026-10-18 sweep.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**RULING (@ligon, 2026-10-20): per-household exposure.**
- **A, in this PR.** Keep the declared, one-constant-per-wave exposure for `period=`. Disclose the shortfall: `attrs['period']` reports, per wave, how many households were asked fewer times than declared, and the implied understatement.
- **Measured** (r2): Burkina 2014, 9.3% of households, −3.94% aggregate under `period=`; GhanaLSS ≤ ~1%.
- **B, a follow-up (new issue):** per-household exposure, from each passage's cover-page interview status.

title: DECISION: recall windows Phase II -- ship period= on food_expenditures/food_quantities with coverage at 28 of 67 cells under Contract B, and refuse period= on food_prices
